# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues

body:
Review requests following the locking/performance discussion, based on the description at head `5db5092cc6a786e48318f567c4d7b571cc554e48`:

1. **Investigate the measured performance regressions before accepting them.** The description currently reports about 13% lower Direct ordinary-read throughput, 31% lower Direct attach/count/dispose throughput, 21% lower Direct legacy single-read transaction throughput, and approximately 6.3× the cost of a new Shared handle around one read compared with the candidate legacy transaction. Please profile the added session/operation guards, allocations and disposal scheduling, and try focused improvements that preserve all ownership/safety invariants and tests. Confirm the small-read results with longer steady-state windows and paired/alternated runs; distinguish evidence from attribution. Publish the final-revision residual costs and obtain an explicit maintainer performance decision. Green CI and scoped safety reviews alone do not accept these tradeoffs. The complete Shared coordinator/cache redesign can remain follow-up work.

2. **Make the locking and binding contract explicit in the PR/user documentation.** “Bound” means that objects obtained through `tx` always execute within exactly that transaction and reject use after completion; ordinary `db` objects remain independent. Writable Direct owns exclusive admission for its host/dependency lifetime, excluding other processes, including read-only Direct. Multiple standalone read-only Direct processes may coexist only while no writer is admitted. Conflicting Direct opens fail rather than queueing for their turn. For Shared, distinguish lifetime admission, native writer ownership, local handle queuing and ordinary snapshot reads. The current new-handle queue covers those handles; it does not consolidate all ordinary/legacy writers into one process participant. Each admitted handle still releases native ownership before the next acquires it, so local queuing alone does not remove the release/acquire pair.

3. **Revisit the admission-wait contract for the new Shared transaction API.** The proposed `_settings.Timeout` patch was technically unsuitable: that property does not exist, and the collection TIMEOUT pragma is a different contract. However, the underlying UX concern remains: a second synchronous begin can wait indefinitely while its caller is the only code able to finish the first handle. The current behavior is allowed by the updated specs, so this is a requested contract improvement, not a claim of spec violation. Please make an explicit API decision before merge: provide an opt-in bounded/cancellable admission path, or explicitly review and track its deferral. A deadline must cover both the process-local gate and native-mutex admission, preserve cleanup/ownership on cancellation, and never be used to cancel or infer the result of an executing commit. Update litedb-org/LiteDB#3064 and litedb-org/LiteDB#3067 consistently if adopting the option; do not merely apply a timeout to one of the two waits.

Follow-ups are now recorded in the upstream repository:

- [litedb-org/LiteDB#3068](https://github.com/litedb-org/LiteDB/issues/3068): opt-in bounded waiting for writable Direct admission, preserving current default opening behavior and distinguishing contention from real errors.
- [litedb-org/LiteDB#3069](https://github.com/litedb-org/LiteDB/issues/3069): reusable per-process/database Shared writer ownership, local scheduling and bounded handoff with remote-process fairness.
- [litedb-org/LiteDB#3017](https://github.com/litedb-org/LiteDB/issues/3017) now explicitly separates participation/mapping/reader-registry consolidation from writer scheduling.
- [litedb-org/LiteDB#3004](https://github.com/litedb-org/LiteDB/issues/3004) now explicitly separates retained engine/cache coherence from holder reuse and lock handoff, with independent measurements/proofs for each.

Please continue final-head safety verification and hosted CI while addressing the review requests. These follow-ups do not require folding the complete Shared redesign into this PR.

Addressed requests 2 and 3 in fe4d1725e (implementation commits 062a2507a and 0f90d1be0):

- PR/user docs now spell out exact binding, Direct dependency-lifetime exclusion and fail-on-conflict behavior, Shared lifetime admission versus native writer ownership/local handle queuing/ordinary snapshots, and the native release/acquire pair between handles.
- Added opt-in `BeginTransaction(TimeSpan sharedAdmissionTimeout, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)`. A single monotonic budget covers local and native waits; cancellation applies only to begin. Specs #3064/#3067 were updated consistently. Existing provider interfaces gain no required members.
- Added local/native and cross-process timeout/cancellation, acquisition cleanup faults, close races, callback/AsyncLocal abandonment and cold-reopen checks. Holder context suppression preserves first-open collation; Windows impersonation is explicitly refused before queuing/acquisition.
- Fixed the hosted disposal starvation failure: cleanup can progress independently of a saturated caller thread pool. A one-worker subprocess fails behaviorally against the earlier implementation and passes after the fix; tests also cover idle/active Direct/Shared close, blocked final release, failed cleanup-thread startup and concurrent retries.

Local safety runs passed 122 tests on net8.0 and 122 on net10.0. All target frameworks build, and the consumer compiled against the actual parent still passes compatibility/capability and error-preservation checks. New hosted checks are running; Windows impersonation execution depends on those runners.

Per the latest instruction, request 1 (profiling, focused improvements and longer paired performance measurements) comes after the correctness work. The old performance table is explicitly historical, and performance acceptance remains outstanding.

Addressed the implementation and evidence requested in [this review](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/pull/133#issuecomment-5899435983), at `c8c0cfab623a22880b1d71eb966b09e89f9153b9`.

1. **Profiled and improved the costs.** The guard/reader changes recover read throughput; independent cleanup-worker reuse removes repeated thread creation while preserving close progress and ownership. The final report includes 52 fresh-process paired runs, every ratio/range, latency/allocation data, default-tiering confirmation and separate profile evidence. Residual costs remain material: Direct reads −8–11%, legacy reads −13–17%, attach/count/dispose −34–52%; a Shared handle around one read costs about 5.7× final legacy. The PR description no longer claims unchanged durable-write performance. **Explicit maintainer performance acceptance is still pending.**
2. **Documented the exact contract.** Bound objects execute in exactly their transaction; ordinary objects stay independent. The PR/user guide now distinguish Direct host-lifetime exclusion, readonly coexistence, conflicting-open refusal, Shared lifetime admission, native writer ownership, handle-only queuing and ordinary snapshots. Each Shared handle still releases/reacquires native ownership.
3. **Added opt-in bounded/cancellable admission.** `BeginTransaction(TimeSpan, CancellationToken)` uses one budget across the local and native waits, cleans partial ownership, and detaches cancellation before returning a handle. It cannot cancel or infer an executing commit. Existing provider interfaces remain unchanged; specs litedb-org/LiteDB#3064 and litedb-org/LiteDB#3067 were updated consistently.

Safety verification also found and fixed thread-pool cleanup starvation and native-holder roots through cancellation callbacks, execution contexts, derived settings and collation. Before/after reproductions, forced release/expiry interleavings, encrypted abandonment, cold indexed/sentinel verification and compatibility checks cover these changes. Final local focused partitions passed 137 tests on each runtime; all target builds passed. Scoped reviewers rechecked their findings, and the final evidence review verified all 52 runs/520 windows.

Final-head hosted validation: [CI](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/actions/runs/36645243860), [Fuzz](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/actions/runs/36645243603), [index-migration compatibility](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/actions/runs/36645243601). All are green on `c8c0cfab6`. The measured production source is `d3ddd94f2`; the final commit changes only documentation, benchmark tooling and evidence.

[Full report and raw evidence](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/blob/codex/transaction-handles/docs/transaction-handles-validation.md). Follow-ups litedb-org/LiteDB#3068, litedb-org/LiteDB#3069, litedb-org/LiteDB#3017 and litedb-org/LiteDB#3004 remain separate.

## Review of PR head `5605290`

Five parallel reviewers covered the handle API, session lifetime, Shared holder reuse, engine internals, and tests/CI. Seven defects were confirmed by running a repro, four of them also compared against the base `49c327cf1`. One was confirmed by tracing the code. One hang was confirmed by a repro but only occurs in an edge case.

The two regressions in the first section should block merging.

### Regressions

**1. Disposing a Shared database while one thread has an open legacy transaction can hang another thread forever.**
Where: [`SessionLifetime.cs:154`](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/blob/560529066aeda64c24d5cdd32d34a8aca12695ae/LiteDB/Client/Transactions/SessionLifetime.cs#L154) together with [`LiteDatabase.cs:425`](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/blob/560529066aeda64c24d5cdd32d34a8aca12695ae/LiteDB/Client/Database/LiteDatabase.cs#L425).

Close only disposes the engine once `_active == 0`. In Shared mode, though, a peer waiting in `SharedMutexOwner.Enter` is only freed by that engine disposal (`_owner.ReleaseAll()`).

Steps:
1. Thread T calls `BeginTrans()` and inserts.
2. Thread U inserts and blocks.
3. T calls `db.Dispose()`.

At head: `Dispose` throws `TimeoutException`, T can no longer Commit or Rollback (`ObjectDisposedException`), U stays blocked, and the cross-process writer mutex stays held until T's thread exits.
At base: Dispose succeeds, and U gets a `LiteException` after about 1 s.

**2. `db.Rebuild()` is starved by ordinary concurrent reads.**
Where: [`OperationLifetime.cs:69-83`](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/blob/560529066aeda64c24d5cdd32d34a8aca12695ae/LiteDB/Engine/Services/OperationLifetime.cs#L69-L83), used by `Rebuild.cs:26`.

`Exclusive()` checks `_active == 0` every 10 ms, but `Enter()` only blocks once `_exclusive` is actually set. New readers are never held back while rebuild waits. The old `EnterExclusive()` stopped new readers as soon as it started waiting.

With 4 reader threads and `TIMEOUT=5s`:

| | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Base | Rebuild succeeds in about 450 ms |
| Head | `LockTimeout("operation/maintenance")` after 5 s |

**3. `LiteEngine.Dispose()` can wait forever.**
Where: [`LiteEngine.cs:235`](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/blob/560529066aeda64c24d5cdd32d34a8aca12695ae/LiteDB/Engine/LiteEngine.cs#L235), which calls `Exclusive(() => true)` with no timeout. The root cause is the same as #2.

- A raw engine with 16 reader threads was still blocked in Dispose after 20 s.
- A peer waiting on a collection lock stalls Dispose for the full lock timeout. On base, Dispose returned in 100 ms.

`LiteDatabase` mostly avoids this because its session close drains work first. Raw `LiteEngine` users hit it directly.

### Other defects

**4. `BeginTransaction()` hangs when the calling thread already holds the Shared lock through another path.**
Where: [`SharedEngine.Transactions.cs:62`](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/blob/560529066aeda64c24d5cdd32d34a8aca12695ae/LiteDB/Client/Shared/SharedEngine.Transactions.cs#L62).

The guard only checks `_owner.IsOwnedByCurrentThread`. It misses two cases:
- A legacy transaction that took over a pin from a streaming reader, i.e. `Execute("SELECT $ …")`, then a write, then `BeginTrans()`.
- An open `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` reader.

In both cases the holder worker waits for a lock that only the blocked caller can release. With the default timeout this never ends; the intended behavior is an immediate `InvalidOperationException`. With a 3 s timeout it fails with `TimeoutException` instead.

**5. Using a bound reader or enumerator after disposing it rolls back the whole transaction.**
Where: [`TransactionEnumerable.cs:21-23`](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/blob/560529066aeda64c24d5cdd32d34a8aca12695ae/LiteDB/Client/Transactions/TransactionEnumerable.cs#L21-L23) and [`:40-44`](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/blob/560529066aeda64c24d5cdd32d34a8aca12695ae/LiteDB/Client/Transactions/TransactionEnumerable.cs#L40-L44).

`Dispose` sets `_inner = null`. A later `Read()`, `MoveNext()` or `Current` then throws `NullReferenceException` inside `Run`, which aborts the handle: the state becomes `Failed` and every earlier write is silently lost.

Ordinary readers throw `ObjectDisposedException` here and leave the transaction alone. Even an `ObjectDisposedException` would still abort the handle through `Run`, so both parts need fixing.

**6. `ILiteTransaction.Dispose()` throws if the database is closing at the same time.**
Where: [`LiteTransaction.cs:216-227`](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/blob/560529066aeda64c24d5cdd32d34a8aca12695ae/LiteDB/Client/Transactions/LiteTransaction.cs#L216-L227).

The state check and `Enter()` happen under separate locks. Depending on timing:
- Close has started but hasn't reached this handle yet: `ObjectDisposedException`.
- The close worker is rolling this handle back right now: `InvalidOperationException("Overlapping transaction disposal…")`.

Either exception masks the one coming out of the `using` body. The bound enumerator and reader `Dispose` behave the same way. The handle still ends up RolledBack, so nothing leaks.

**7. Disposing a healthy handle rethrows another transaction's fatal error.**
Where: [`LiteTransaction.cs:249`](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/blob/560529066aeda64c24d5cdd32d34a8aca12695ae/LiteDB/Client/Transactions/LiteTransaction.cs#L249), leading to `:155-163`.

`Abort` skips the rollback when the engine is already disposed (`onlyIfActive: true`), but `Dispose`/`RollbackCore` does not.

Example: tx2's commit hits an injected disk-write failure, which stops the Direct host. `tx1.Dispose()` then throws tx2's `IOException`.

**8. A stale `<db>-tmp` sort file is no longer deleted (low severity).**
Where: [`SortDisk.cs:111`](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/blob/560529066aeda64c24d5cdd32d34a8aca12695ae/LiteDB/Engine/Sort/SortDisk.cs#L111).

The file is now only deleted if the current engine instance spilled to it. A `-tmp` file left behind by a crashed process stays until some later process spills.

### Test and CI gaps

**Vacuous test:** [`TransactionHandleProcess_Tests.cs:110-111`](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/blob/560529066aeda64c24d5cdd32d34a8aca12695ae/LiteDB.Tests/Internals/TransactionHandleProcess_Tests.cs#L110-L111). The test asserts the child is blocked only 100 ms after it prints `attempting`. An unblocked child takes about 165 ms to finish anyway, so the test passes even if cross-process waiting is broken.
Fix: print a marker from `TransactionAdmission.Observe("native-wait")` and wait for it before asserting.

**Weak (plausible):** `TransactionHandleLifetime_Tests.cs:100` and `:127` accept `ObjectDisposedException`. On a slow runner they can pass without exercising the "cancel pending begin" path.
Fix: gate on `Observe` counts and require `OperationCanceledException`.

**No .NET Framework coverage of Shared wrapper reuse:** all of `TransactionHandleChild*_Tests` is `#if !NETFRAMEWORK`. ChildLifetime and ChildSettings are excluded only because their helpers live in the ChildReuse file, and they compile for net462 once the helpers are moved. The netstandard2.0 build also skips the `NET8_0_OR_GREATER` coordination reset.

**Untested behavior:**
- Several handles running concurrently in Direct mode; tests and fuzzing are sequential only.
- Drop or rename on a writable handle.
- `$cols` / `$indexes` queries through a handle.
- Rejection of custom `ILiteEngine`s; only the manual tool checks it.
- The same-thread legacy-transaction guard.

**Undocumented public break:** using a disposed `LiteDatabase` now throws `ObjectDisposedException` instead of `LiteException(ENGINE_DISPOSED)`. The migration section of `docs/transaction-handles.md` doesn't mention this.

### Checked and found sound

- **Binding:** no collection, query, Include, vector or SQL path runs outside the handle.
- **Handle concurrency:** overlapping use and callback reentry are detected correctly.
- **Shared holder:** no page cache survives between handles, the mutex is released on the thread that acquired it, no job is lost when a pool worker retires, and settings invalidation is complete.
- **Test edits:** the changes to existing tests are justified.
- **Test runs:** the scoped test suite passed 218/218, including repeated runs under full CPU load.

body:
**Reviewed commit:** `eb01f346eb7d8d51925a45c2f87ef40e1c3984ee` — the head at review time, which only touched tests/harness/docs after `0108213`.

**Headline:** the two P2 findings from the prior review (the unprotected `pin.WaitReleased()` in `SharedEngine.Disposal.cs`, and the Shared final-checkpoint paths that still discard/swallow errors despite the migration guide's propagation claim) are unchanged at this head. I found one new P2 and several P3 robustness items; none is an acknowledged-commit-loss counterexample.

**New P2 — Shared mutex waits became 10 ms polls.** `SharedMutexTurnstile.WaitCancellable` polls `WaitOne(10)` whenever the token is cancellable, and `SessionEngine.Call` installs the session's always-cancellable `Closing` token on every ordinary call, so every Shared owner/pin/turnstile acquisition now polls instead of blocking. That adds latency and drops the waiter out of the kernel queue between polls (the old `TakeGate` comment warned about exactly this). `WaitHandle.WaitAny(mutex, closing.WaitHandle)` would keep it blocking and cancellable. This plausibly feeds the Shared read regressions in the PR table.

**P3 items:**
- `LiteTransaction.Commit` labels any pre-persist exception `Indeterminate` and releases resources, but in Direct mode the handle shares the facade's `EngineContext` (refcounted), so a still-Active engine transaction keeps its locks until the facade closes. Narrow today, but one precondition away from a lock leak.
- `CollectionLock` self-wait detection is `null`ed for handle-owned locks, so the documented "ordinary objects in callbacks" pattern can hang for the full 60 s `TIMEOUT` instead of failing fast.
- Cached Shared child reuse re-validates only Password/Collation; the `ReadTransform` weak wrapper stays bound to the first begin's delegate.
- `SharedHolderScheduler` and `SessionCloseScheduler` are the same 117 lines apart from names.
- `LiteEngine.Close()` takes an unbounded `Exclusive` lease, and the maintenance fence can deadlock an active op that depends on fresh work from another thread once close is requested.
